cohort: Pregnant women treated for bowel endometriosis (n=71) were matched 1:3 with healthy pregnant women (n=213) based on parity, age, BMI, and gestational age, at a single tertiary-care university hospital.
finding: Women treated for bowel endometriosis are more exposed to adverse pregnancy outcomes, including labor abnormalities, increased cesarean section rates, and various hemorrhagic complications, as well as adverse neonatal outcomes such as higher NICU admission rates, compared to healthy controls.
mod_finding: The risk of cesarean section, including emergent cesarean sections, was significantly higher in women treated for bowel endometriosis.
